title: Short: "The summit is a seabed"

lines.text: Pick up a stone from the very top of Mount Everest, and look closely.
Crinoids and brachiopods, the remains of sea creatures.
lines.cue: caption: SEA CREATURES, AT THE TOP

lines.text: The summit is limestone, laid down in a warm, shallow sea about four hundred and fifty million years ago.
lines.cue: caption: A SEABED, 450 MILLION YEARS OLD

lines.text: Now that seafloor sits almost nine kilometres above the ocean.
Something pushed it up there, over about fifty million years.
It's still rising, about two millimetres every year.
lines.cue: caption: STILL RISING: 2 MM A YEAR

lines.text: And yet it will never get much higher than this.
So what stops a mountain from climbing? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
